ANY REGIME: a swept LOW is more often a fake and sweeps deeper than a swept HIGH (real 16-20 % vs 25-26 %; 90 % of fakes within 1.65-2.04 vs 1.21-1.31 M5 ATR; 1 ATR past: real 45 % vs 66-71 %) - so fading a break up already 1 ATR past a high is at a disadvantage, while a break down 1 ATR past a low still often comes back (the fade of a low keeps more of its edge). The 24-hour state (trend / sideways) changed the fake / real split little. BEAR and MIXED regimes: too few days in the design years to say (42 bear days); the replay months (mostly bear days) showed sells near 0 and buys -0.02 to -0.07 - information only. H4 AND H1 DOWN = the PULLBACK of the bull market: a sell is at its greatest disadvantage there (M5 -0.18 R, M1 -0.21), and buying a swept low that closes back has the best edge of every cell on M5 (+0.044 R, 60 % win; following a high's break +0.019, 60 %) - it is the moment to prepare a BUY at the pullback's bottom, not to sell. No H4 / H1 combination gives a bull-regime sell the edge in both methods (two single cells +0.002 and +0.053, the other method losing there). On M1 every bare trigger loses in every cell (-0.06 to -0.22: the stops are small, the spread is a larger part of the risk), the buys always above the sells of the same cell.
